details: The United States launched limited "defensive" strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, targeting surface-to-air missiles allegedly used against US assets. This occurred on the eve of crucial US midterm elections. Simultaneously, US and Iranian officials have signaled growing optimism for a potential deal to de-escalate the conflict, with Iran's Foreign Minister indicating a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be implemented within two days if demands are met. This diplomatic acceleration, coming less than 24 hours after the strikes, led to a fall in Brent crude oil prices.
title: US Conducts 'Defensive' Strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island Amid Diplomatic Efforts

details: Russia has continued its intensified attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, causing power outages for hundreds of thousands of homes. Amnesty International warned that these increased strikes risk creating a new humanitarian catastrophe ahead of winter. A localized truce in Ukraine's Kherson region, brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump, ended on Sunday night, with fighting reportedly resuming elsewhere.
title: Russia Continues Strikes on Ukraine's Energy Infrastructure, Truce Ends

details: North Korea has been identified by experts, including the FBI, as the likely culprit behind a record $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft from the Binance exchange on or about October 29th. Investors subsequently pulled $3.6 billion in funds from Binance, though the platform has since begun a phased reopening and committed to covering all customer losses. This incident highlights the significant security risks and illicit financing activities within the crypto space.
title: North Korea Blamed for Record $6.3 Billion Binance Crypto Hack

details: Global financial markets are experiencing fragility due to persistent wars, soaring sovereign debt, and trade tensions. Signs of trouble include selloffs in Japanese and French bonds and plunging emerging-market currencies. The artificial intelligence (AI) trade, which had been a source of optimism, is also starting to show cracks, with investors growing nervous about market resiliency. US President Donald Trump's trade policies and the Iran war's energy shock have revived inflation, pressuring central banks to raise interest rates and increasing borrowing costs.
title: Global Markets Fragile as AI Trade Shows Cracks Amid Geopolitical Tensions
